newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Linde predicts improved earnings for 1997.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Linde predicts improved earnings for 1997.

text.p: German plant and engineering group Linde AG said on Tuesday it expected to report improved earnings and sales for 1997 after revenue rose 6.4 percent in the first four months of the year.

Linde chief executive Hans Meinhardt, who stepped down from the position on Tuesday after 21 years at the helm of Linde, told the group's annual general meeting that 1997 growth in sales and earnings would be similar to that seen in 1996.
Linde's sales in 1996, the best in company history, rose 6.2 percent to 8.8 billion marks ($5.2 billion) while net profit rose 10.4 percent to 396 million marks.
The Munich-based group reported four-month sales of 2.749 billion marks and said its incoming orders in the period rose 12 percent to 3.143 billion marks.
Incoming orders for the first four months of the year were up 12 percent at 3.14 billion marks over year-ago levels, while orders in hand totalled 6.6 billion marks, a 5.5 percent rise.
Linde also plans to invest about one billion marks in 1997, about the same as the record one billion marks last year.

Meinhardt, who will be replaced by 60-year-old Gerhard Full and will now join the supervisory board, said growth would continue to come from foreign business and would keep up cost-cutting measures to improve earnings.
Meinhardt said Linde would seek to build its market position in Europe, Southeast Asia and the United States, helping to raise the share of foreign sales at the group.
Linde is aiming to raise its sales in the medium term to 14 billion marks based on its current four business areas -- plant construction, hydraulics, refrigeration technology and technical gases.
But Meinhardt repeated that Linde also aimed to add a fifth core business area. He said future growth would come within the Linde group but also through acquisitions.
He also said Linde would wait for the start of European currency union, slated to begin in January 1999, before redenominating its shares.
Linde shares have a nominal value of 50 marks.
"When the euro comes, Linde will redenominate its shares," Linde chief executive Hans Meinhardt said in response to a question at the group's annual general meeting.
Many publically-listed German companies have redenominated their shares to a nominal value of five marks.
